breadcrumb.name: UAE Green Visa Eligibility: The Smart Way to Live in the UAE in 2026

contentHtml:
If you want to build a life in the UAE without being locked into a single employer, the Green Visa deserves your attention. It is designed for

  • Professionals
  • Feelancers
  • Investors
  • Self-employed

Who seek freedom, flexibility, and long-term presence.

The experts at The UAE GATE prepared this detailed article on the UAE Green Visa.  We utilise official sources (including icp.gov.ae or gdrfad.gov.ae) and the latest updates as of early 2026 to provide accurate information.

Begin With A Clear Look at the UAE Green Visa

The UAE Green Visa was introduced to support the country’s shift toward a knowledge-based economy. This visa facilitates a 5-year, renewable residence permit built around self-sponsorship. This means an individual with a green visa can live, work, and invest in the UAE independently.

There is no need for a national sponsor or employer. The intent of the green visa is clear: attract global talent and support long-term innovation.

Green Visa Eligibility: Who Can Apply

It is evident from above that freelancers, skilled employees, and business investors can apply for the UAE Visa. Below, we have mentioned the specific requirements for each category. 

1. Skilled Workers

  • Employment contract in the UAE.
  • Minimum bachelor’s degree or equivalent.
  • Monthly salary of at least AED 15,000 (or equivalent).
  • Classified in occupational levels 1, 2, or 3 by MOHRE.

2. Investors and Business Partners

  • Proof of investment or partnership in a UAE-based project or commercial activity.
  • All required licenses and approvals from relevant local authorities.
  • ICP approval based on the investor rating system.
  • If multiple licences are held, total invested capital is considered.

3. Freelancers and/or Self-Employed 

  • Freelance or self-employment permit from MOHRE.
  • Must have a Bachelor’s degree or specialised diploma.
  • Show consistent annual earnings of AED 360,000, or provide proof of financial self-support.

Let’s understand the cost associated with the UAE Green Visa.

UAE Green Visa: Costs and Fees [as of early 2026]

In the subsequent section, we break down the general cost structure of the UAE Green Visa. According to the sources, the fees vary by emirate and application type. So, it is always advisable to confirm the final amount on the ICP or GDRFA portal.

Cost Component Estimated Amount (AED)
Residence visa issuance 200–500 + VAT
Medical fitness test 320–500
Emirates ID (5 years) 575–1,150 (depending on validity).
Knowledge Dirham fee 10
Innovation Dirham fee 10
Inside-country status change (if applicable) 500
Total estimated cost (main applicant) 3,000–5,000

Table 1.1 UAE Green Visa Pricing 

Additional notes

  • Family sponsorship involves similar fees per dependent.
  • Overstay fine after the grace period is AED 50 per day.

Prime Benefits of the Green Visa

The Green Visa modernises long-term living in the UAE with greater autonomy. Its benefits focus on independence, stability, and continuity.

Here is what it offers:

  • Self-sponsorship and flexibility
    There is no requirement for a local employer or sponsor. This allows holders to change jobs freely or pursue independent work.
  • Family sponsorship
    Holders can sponsor their family. This includes a spouse, sons (up to age 25), unmarried daughters (no age limit), and children with special needs (no age limit). Family members receive the same 5-year validity.
  • Access to growth sectors
    Provides entry into high-growth sectors, including technology and finance.
  • 5-year renewability
    Renewable for another 5 years ifthe  original eligibility criteria are still met.
  • Grace period support
    Additional time is provided after expiry or cancellation to regularise residency status.

UAE Green Visa: Essential Documents Checklist

Documentation varies by category but generally includes:

  • Passport copy (valid for at least six months)
  • Photograph.
  • Employment contract, salary proof, attested degree, MoHRE classification (Skilled workers)
  • MOHRE permit, income proof, attested qualifications (Freelancers/self-employed)
  • Investment/partnership agreement, trade license, and authority approvals (Investors/partners)

Important Note: Arabic or English should be the document’s language. Moreover, foreign qualifications/degrees usually require attestation.
